summary.goal: Implement PlannerLead as a persistent agent service that connects to agent-relay as a RelayClient (not spawn), listens for channel messages, uses Anthropic API to generate intelligent responses, and can read/modify plans via the planner API. Runs integrated with planner-core backend.
summary.context: The original relay-planning-agent feature used agent-relay's spawn() function, which is designed for task-oriented CLI workers that execute and exit. For an always-on planning assistant, we need a different pattern: a persistent Node.js service that connects as a RelayClient, sets up message handlers, and stays running indefinitely. This matches how agent-relay is actually designed to work.
in_scope: Receives and responds to channel messages
Uses Anthropic API for intelligent responses
Tool use: read_plan, list_plans, add_step, edit_step

acceptance_criteria.description: PlannerLead connects to agent-relay automatically when planner-core backend starts
PlannerLead joins #planner channel on startup and announces availability
PlannerLead joins #plan-{id} channels when plans are created or when explicitly invited
Messages sent to PlannerLead's channels are received and trigger response generation
PlannerLead uses Anthropic API with appropriate system prompt to generate contextual responses
PlannerLead can read plan data using read_plan tool when users ask about specific plans
PlannerLead can modify plans (add_step, edit_step) when users request changes
Conversation history is maintained per-channel for contextual follow-up responses
PlannerLead reconnects automatically when agent-relay connection is lost
Response latency is under 10 seconds (API call time, not spawn overhead)

steps.title: Add @anthropic-ai/sdk dependency
steps.description: Install the Anthropic SDK for direct API access. This enables calling Claude models programmatically with full control over system prompts, tools, and conversation history.

acceptance_criteria.description: @anthropic-ai/sdk is added to package.json dependencies
Package installs successfully with npm install
TypeScript types are available for Anthropic client

steps.title: Create Anthropic client configuration
steps.description: Create src/relay/anthropic-config.ts with configuration for the Anthropic client. Reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from environment. Exports configured client instance and model constants.

acceptance_criteria.description: Exports getAnthropicClient() that returns configured Anthropic instance
Reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from process.env
Exports MODEL constant (claude-sonnet-4-20250514 or similar)
Logs warning if API key is missing (does not throw - allows mock mode)

steps.title: Define PlannerLead tool schemas
steps.description: Create src/relay/planner-lead-tools.ts defining the tool schemas for Anthropic tool use. Tools: read_plan (get plan by ID), list_plans (list all plans), add_step (add step to plan), edit_step (modify existing step). Use Zod for validation.

acceptance_criteria.description: Exports PLANNER_LEAD_TOOLS array in Anthropic tool format: [{ name: string, description: string, input_schema: JSONSchema }]
read_plan tool: input { plan_id: string }, returns plan summary with goal, status, step count
list_plans tool: input { status?: 'draft'|'approved'|'published' }, returns array of { plan_id, goal, status }
add_step tool: input { plan_id, title, description, scope?, dependencies?: string[] }, returns created step_id
edit_step tool: input { plan_id, step_id, title?, description?, dependencies? }, returns updated step

steps.title: Implement tool execution handlers
steps.description: Add tool execution logic to planner-lead-tools.ts. Each handler receives tool input, calls the appropriate storage/domain methods, and returns the result. Handlers need access to storage (passed via closure or parameter).

acceptance_criteria.description: Exports executeTool(toolName, input, storage) function
read_plan handler: calls storage.getPlan(), storage.getLatestVersion(), returns { plan_id, goal, status, steps: [{ step_id, title }] } or error
list_plans handler: calls storage.listPlans(), returns [{ plan_id, goal, status, step_count }]
add_step handler: gets latest version, adds step via domain logic, returns { step_id, title }
edit_step handler: gets version, finds step, updates via domain logic, returns updated step
All handlers return { success: true, result: ... } or { success: false, error: string }

steps.title: Create conversation history manager
steps.description: Create src/relay/conversation-history.ts to manage per-channel conversation history. Stores messages in memory with channel ID as key. Implements sliding window to prevent context overflow (keep last N messages or tokens).

acceptance_criteria.description: Exports ConversationHistory class or module
addMessage(channelId, role: 'user'|'assistant', content) appends to channel history
getHistory(channelId) returns array of { role, content } for Anthropic messages format
Implements max message limit (e.g., 50 messages per channel) with FIFO eviction

Describes PlannerLead as a planning assistant
Lists available tools and when to use them

Exports initPlannerLead(storage) that connects and sets up handlers
onChannelMessage handler receives (from, channel, body, envelope)
Auto-joins #planner channel on successful connection

Exports terminatePlannerLead() for graceful shutdown

steps.title: Implement message handling and response generation
steps.description: Add message handling logic to PlannerLead. When a channel message is received: (1) add to conversation history, (2) call Anthropic API with history + tools, (3) handle tool_use blocks by executing tools, (4) send response back to channel.

acceptance_criteria.description: handleChannelMessage(from, channel, body) is called for each incoming message
Adds user message to conversation history for that channel
Calls Anthropic messages API with: model, system prompt, history, tools
If response contains tool_use blocks: executes each tool, collects results, continues conversation
Extracts final text response and sends via client.sendChannelMessage()

acceptance_criteria.description: When createPlanChannel(planId) is called, PlannerLead joins the new channel

steps.title: Update server startup integration
steps.description: Update src/server.ts to initialize PlannerLead with the new pattern. Pass storage instance to initPlannerLead. Update shutdown sequence to call terminatePlannerLead.

acceptance_criteria.description: initPlannerLead(storage) is called after relay connection attempt
PlannerLead initializes even if relay is disconnected (will connect when available)

steps.title: Add mock mode for PlannerLead
steps.description: When ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set or relay is unavailable, PlannerLead should operate in mock mode. In mock mode, it still joins channels but responds with helpful mock messages instead of calling Anthropic API.

design_decisions.decision: Use RelayClient pattern instead of spawn()
design_decisions.rationale: spawn() is for task-oriented CLI workers that exit. RelayClient is the correct pattern for persistent agents that listen for messages.
Simpler deployment, shared database access, easier to manage lifecycle. Can extract to separate process later if needed.
Direct API call gives us control over system prompt, tools, conversation history. Lower latency than spawning CLI tools.
Simpler implementation, sufficient for initial use. Can add persistence to SQLite later.
Prevents PlannerLead from responding to every message in channels, which would be noisy. Users explicitly invoke the assistant when needed.
